title: jmap-server: /set localizations validation, stale-translation pruning, updated echo
description:
jmap-server: /set for localizable types.
- On create and update: run jmap_types::i18n::check_localizations.
- On update: compute which base localizable properties changed and which localizations paths the patch touched, then run prune_stale.
- When pruning changed anything, include `localizations` in that object's `updated` entry (RFC 8620 5.3, server-changed properties). Only do this for callers with i18n in `using`; others never see the property.
- Base-only rules stay base-only: sibling uniqueness etc. is checked on base values. Localized values get the same length and syntax limits (draft SHOULD).
- Optional per-object cap on the number of localizations, reported as invalidProperties.
- Works with the conditional epic (JMAP-y1yu): pruning is part of the same atomic update.
Tests: a client without i18n renames -> translations pruned; a client updating only localizations/fr/name while renaming -> de pruned, fr kept.
notes:
Design: docs/design/updates.md (final 2026-11-15, decisions 27-31). Pruning runs for every client; echo localizations (full post-prune value) in updated only to i18n clients. locale-only change prunes nothing (G3). Cap via I18nInfo::max_localizations.
Done 2026-11-15. Split: backends apply /set patches here (update_object takes the patch), so the post-patch checks and pruning are jmap_server::localized_update, which a backend MUST call inside update_object and, when it returns true, return Ok(Some(obj)) so localizations is echoed. Handlers use I18nSet::{check_create, check_patch, echo}. Wiring into Mailbox/AddressBook/Principal/Calendar handlers and memory backends is .7-.10. Atomic with conditional by construction (runs inside the backend update).
close_reason: I18nSet (handler gate/check/echo) and localized_update (backend check+prune in the atomic update); 13 tests
